title: Here's where I got to with one month of Claude Max.
author: rutan668
selftext:
Why a bunch of images rather than the Claude artefact it came from?  That would be because ending a Claude subscription ends your access to Claude code - all the chats and all the artefacts!  All gone.  If Claude could have made me money I could have paid to continue the Claude Max subscription, but it wasn't to be.  BTW this is an older version of the artefact which I luckily used to create a PDF from.  The open stuff is now closed.  
  
I didn't make it but I thought I got close and if you can use it to help you on your journey and you make it then have a thought for me when you're sipping a martini on your private jet.

comments.author: ochimaru420
comments.body:
Thanks for sharing!  I read through Claude's presentation, and I'm reading that this is targeting lag from BTC to MSTR?  It's a great idea, in theory, but the report seems to say all 4 bots failed bc the lag was too fast.  Only a live test could prove it and may just end up following the MSTR trend regardless as there's other factors impacting their price.

I've discovered that most backtests that sound impressive are based on logical fallacies and don't even compare to the live results.  So it's all imaginary.  As soon as you ask for the raw data and verify the logic you'll see a rabbithole of flaws.  In your case it would depend on the btc exchange used, their lag, the fee spread, the broker used and spread of MSTR within the timeframe as well as the difference between your data sources and the exchange/brokers used.  There's probably 10 more layers of assumptions under that.

Since the most granular free data is only 1m level and prices move a lot "intra bar" a lot more happens than is visible.  Claude also corrupts strategies with it's own genius assumptions.  It loves to claim a breakthrough only to have it disproved moments later, or an edge that is an coincidence or outlier.  It loves to tell me my strategy doesn't work only for me to prove again and again that it does.

I find it's better to treat it as an employee to run reports and code.  Like a college graduate that's really smart but doesn't have any real world experience.
